summary: Saturday arXiv check: no fresh Saturday submission batch was available, so the relevant recent window is the Friday, 7 August 2026 listing plus recent high-signal physics AI/ML submissions. The strongest heavy-ion-adjacent experimental result is ALICE three-proton femtoscopy as a three-body hadronic-interaction probe. The strongest dense-QCD theory/phenomenology item is the Lee-Yang-edge reconstruction of the QCD chiral crossover line. The strongest HEP ML use is the CMS graph-network semivisible-jet search. NestyNet and Kastor are the most transferable scientific-ML method papers, while the Lyapunov-exponent estimator is included only as a caution because experimental validation is still future work.
strongest_paper_summary: ALICE arXiv:2608.05708 is the strongest directly relevant nuclear/HEP result in the recent window: it measures three-proton correlations at 13.6 TeV and uses femtoscopy to probe three-body hadronic dynamics with explicit background and detector corrections.

papers.title: Three-baryon femtoscopy as an effective 3->3 scattering experiment
papers.abstract: ALICE measures the three-proton correlation function in pp collisions at sqrt(s)=13.6 TeV and introduces an analysis strategy to isolate the p-p-p contribution after correcting background channels and detector effects. The observable is compared to three-body continuum calculations and is reported to be sensitive to partial-wave structure in the nucleon-nucleon interaction.

papers.title: QCD Chiral Crossover Line from Lee-Yang Edge Singularities
papers.authors_short: Heng-Tong Ding, Swagato Mukherjee, Peter Petreczky, Kai-Fan Ye
papers.abstract: The paper reconstructs the QCD chiral crossover line from Lee-Yang edge singularities in the complex baryon chemical potential plane, mapping lattice-extracted Lee-Yang-zero estimates to the universal chiral Lee-Yang edge. The resulting curvature is consistent with continuum lattice-QCD results at small mu_B without using that expansion as input.

papers.title: ePIC Early Science Report
papers.authors_short: D. Abbott, N. Abdelrahman, S. Abhijit, I. Abualrob, R. B. Achari, and the ePIC Collaboration
papers.abstract: The ePIC Collaboration outlines early EIC measurements using realistic early-running beam configurations and detailed Geant4 detector simulation, digitization, and reconstruction. It spans inclusive, semi-inclusive, exclusive, diffractive, tagging, jet, and heavy-flavor measurements in electron-proton and electron-ion collisions.

papers.title: Anisotropy effects on heavy quark dynamics in Gribov modified gluon plasma
papers.authors_short: Sumit, Jai Prakash, Santosh Kumar Das, Najmul Haque
papers.abstract: This revised paper studies charm and bottom transport in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma using a nonperturbative Gribov-resummed framework within a Fokker-Planck treatment. Drag and diffusion coefficients are propagated to heavy-quark energy loss and nuclear modification factors including elastic and inelastic collisions.

papers.title: Search for resonant production of lepton-enriched semivisible jets in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s) = 13 TeV
papers.abstract: CMS searches 138 fb^-1 of 13 TeV pp data for lepton-enriched semivisible jets. The analysis uses a graph neural network for jet identification and a fully connected neural network that combines jet- and event-level information, setting first constraints on lepton-enriched semivisible jets.

papers.title: NestyNet. I. Physics Functions Are Hard to Fit with Neural Networks: A Framework for Accurate Surrogates and Analytic Derivatives
papers.authors_short: Rodrigo Ibata, Wassim Tenachi, Foivos Diakogiannis, Neil Ibata, Anirudh Shankar
papers.abstract: NestyNet is a deterministic segmented analytic surrogate with a tailored Levenberg-Marquardt optimizer for stiff physics functions. It reports large median improvements over standard neural networks on AI Feynman function values and derivatives, while providing analytic gradients, Hessians, Laplacians, and antiderivatives.

papers.title: Kastor: An efficient fine-tuning strategy for generative emulation of PDE simulations
papers.authors_short: Guillaume Couairon, Alexis Jacq, Yu-Han Wu, Renu Singh, Yana Hasson, Quentin Berthet, Romuald Elie
papers.abstract: Kastor adapts a deterministic physics foundation model into a generative PDE surrogate with large-stride autoregression, temporal super-resolution, mean-prediction regularization, and spatial-gradient matching. It reports improved forecasting accuracy, spectral consistency, and computational efficiency on The Well benchmark.

papers.title: Machine Learning is Good for Physics - and Vice Versa
papers.abstract: A perspective article on how scientific AI interacts with fundamental-physics methodology, emphasizing statistical validation and theory-level generalization as central standards for new-physics discovery in large datasets.

cautions.title: Equation-Free Period-Aware Forecast-Error Contraction for Estimating Negative Largest Lyapunov Exponents from Short Trajectory Ensembles
cautions.authors_short: Andrei Velichko, N'Gbo N'Gbo, Viet-Thanh Pham
cautions.abstract: The method estimates dominant negative Lyapunov exponents from short scalar trajectory ensembles using period-aware forecast-error contraction. It performs well on controlled maps, but the abstract states that experimental validation remains future work.
cautions.reason: Potentially useful for stability diagnostics, but transfer to HEP, detector operations, or heavy-ion dynamics is speculative until tested on experimental or simulator-derived data with realistic noise and systematics.
